title: WA Telecom Admin — Pretest B
description: 30-question NEC 2023 book-reference pretest. Distribution: Introduction 2; General Requirements 3; Grounding and Bonding 3; Wiring Methods 3; Hazardous Locations 1; Special Conditions 4; Communications Systems 8; General Trade Knowledge and Theory 6. Questions differ from Pretest A.

questions.question: Which installation is not covered by the Code?
choices: Installations in ships, watercraft other than floating buildings, railway rolling stock, aircraft, or automotive vehicles other than mobile homes and recreational vehicles
Wiring in a commercial office building
Electrical conductors connecting equipment to a premises supply
questions.answer: Installations in ships, watercraft other than floating buildings, railway rolling stock, aircraft, or automotive vehicles other than mobile homes and recreational vehicles
questions.explanation: This group of installations is expressly identified as not covered. Reference: 90.2(D)(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Who has responsibility for interpreting Code rules, deciding on approval of equipment and materials, and granting contemplated special permission?
questions.explanation: These responsibilities are assigned to the authority having jurisdiction for Code enforcement. Reference: 90.4(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: A branch circuit consists of the circuit conductors between the final overcurrent device protecting the circuit and the ______.
questions.explanation: The Article 100 definition places the branch-circuit conductors between the final overcurrent device and the outlet or outlets. Reference: Article 100, Branch Circuit, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Which description is part of the Code definition of listed equipment, materials, or services?
choices: They are included in a list published by an organization acceptable to the authority having jurisdiction and concerned with evaluation of products or services
They are selected only because they have the lowest purchase price
They are approved solely by the installer without evaluation
They are manufactured outside the jurisdiction and need no inspection
questions.answer: They are included in a list published by an organization acceptable to the authority having jurisdiction and concerned with evaluation of products or services
questions.explanation: This choice states the opening requirement of the Article 100 definition of Listed. Reference: Article 100, Listed, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Conductors and equipment required or permitted by the Code are acceptable only when what condition is met?
choices: They are less than one year old
They are installed by the manufacturer
They are painted with an identifying color
questions.explanation: The general approval rule states that required or permitted conductors and equipment are acceptable only if approved. Reference: 110.2, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes earth in relation to an effective ground-fault current path?
choices: Earth must not be considered an effective ground-fault current path
Earth is always the only permitted ground-fault current path
Earth replaces the equipment grounding conductor in every installation
Earth is the normal return path for all branch-circuit current
questions.answer: Earth must not be considered an effective ground-fault current path
questions.explanation: The grounding and bonding performance rule expressly states that earth is not an effective ground-fault current path. Reference: 250.4(A)(5), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: A single rod, pipe, or plate grounding electrode generally requires a supplemental electrode unless its resistance to earth is ______.
questions.explanation: The supplemental-electrode exception applies where a single rod, pipe, or plate electrode has a resistance to earth of 25 ohms or less. Reference: 250.53(A)(2), Exception, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What conductor length and minimum size are required for a copper ground ring encircling a building or structure?
choices: At least 6.0 m (20 ft) of bare copper not smaller than 2 AWG
At least 3.0 m (10 ft) of insulated copper not smaller than 14 AWG
At least 1.8 m (6 ft) of bare copper not smaller than 10 AWG
At least 15 m (50 ft) of aluminum not smaller than 6 AWG
questions.answer: At least 6.0 m (20 ft) of bare copper not smaller than 2 AWG
questions.explanation: A ground ring consists of at least 6.0 m (20 ft) of bare copper conductor not smaller than 2 AWG in direct contact with earth. Reference: 250.52(A)(4), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: May cables and raceways above a suspended ceiling be supported by the ceiling grid?
choices: No, cables and raceways must not be supported by ceiling grids
Yes, if the cable is under 50 volts
Yes, if plastic cable ties are used
questions.answer: No, cables and raceways must not be supported by ceiling grids
questions.explanation: The general securing-and-supporting rule states that cables and raceways must not be supported by ceiling grids. Reference: 300.11(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: How must openings around electrical penetrations through fire-resistance-rated walls, partitions, floors, or ceilings be treated?
choices: They must be firestopped using approved methods to maintain the fire-resistance rating
They may be left open for ventilation
They need only be covered with ordinary tape
They must be filled only with wood blocking
questions.answer: They must be firestopped using approved methods to maintain the fire-resistance rating
questions.explanation: The NEC requires approved firestopping methods that maintain the fire-resistance rating. Reference: 300.21, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: When a raceway or cable contains four through six current-carrying conductors, what adjustment factor applies to the table ampacity before any necessary ambient-temperature correction?
questions.explanation: The adjustment-factor table assigns 80 percent to four through six current-carrying conductors. Reference: Table 310.15(C)(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What makes a location a Class II hazardous location?
choices: It is hazardous because of the presence of combustible dust
It contains only flammable gases or vapors
It is hazardous only because its equipment exceeds 1000 volts
questions.answer: It is hazardous because of the presence of combustible dust
questions.explanation: Class II locations are those hazardous because of the presence of combustible dust. Reference: 500.5(C), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Critical operations power system wiring must be protected against physical damage. Which wiring method is specifically permitted?
choices: Flexible cord laid on the floor
questions.explanation: Rigid metal conduit is one of the specifically permitted wiring methods for COPS wiring protected against physical damage. Reference: 708.10(C)(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: A cable is marked CL4P. What cable type does the marking identify?
questions.explanation: The cable-marking table identifies CL4P as Class 4 plenum cable. Reference: Table 722.179(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Class 2 circuit conductors are installed in the same cable with Class 3 circuit conductors. What insulation is required for the Class 2 conductors?
choices: Insulation at least that required for the Class 3 circuit
No insulation when the cable is listed
Insulation rated only for the Class 2 source
questions.answer: Insulation at least that required for the Class 3 circuit
questions.explanation: Class 2 conductors installed with Class 3 conductors must have insulation at least that required for the Class 3 circuit. Reference: 725.139(C), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What is the maximum output voltage permitted for a Class 4 power transmitter?
questions.explanation: A Class 4 circuit must be supplied by a transmitter having an output of not more than 450 volts peak or dc. Reference: 726.121, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Exposed communications cables installed on ceiling or sidewall surfaces must be supported in what manner?
choices: By the building structure so the cable will not be damaged by normal building use
By laying them directly on removable ceiling panels
Only by attachment to sprinkler piping
By taping them to any available raceway
questions.answer: By the building structure so the cable will not be damaged by normal building use
questions.explanation: Exposed communications cables on ceilings and sidewalls must be supported by the building structure so normal building use will not damage them. Reference: 800.24(A), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What must be done around communications cable penetrations through fire-resistance-rated assemblies?
choices: Use approved firestopping methods to maintain the fire-resistance rating
Use ordinary packing material without approval
Cover only the visible side with paint
questions.answer: Use approved firestopping methods to maintain the fire-resistance rating
questions.explanation: Communications cable and raceway penetrations must be firestopped using approved methods that maintain the rating. Reference: 800.26, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Communications wires and cables passing above a roof generally require a vertical clearance of not less than ______ from all points of the roof over which they pass.
questions.explanation: The general above-roof clearance is not less than 2.5 m (8 ft), subject to the listed exceptions. Reference: 800.44(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Where practicable, what separation must be maintained between lightning-protection conductors and communications wires, communications cables, and CATV-type coaxial cables on buildings?
questions.explanation: Where practicable, the required separation from lightning-protection conductors is at least 1.8 m (6 ft). Reference: 800.53, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: An interbuilding communications circuit on a premises has lightning exposure. Where must listed primary protectors be installed?
choices: At each end of the interbuilding circuit
Only at the building with the larger service
Nowhere if the cable is longer than 42 m (140 ft)
questions.answer: At each end of the interbuilding circuit
questions.explanation: Where lightning exposure exists, each interbuilding communications circuit on a premises must be protected by a listed primary protector at each end. Reference: 805.90(A), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Where must a receiving-station antenna discharge unit be located?
choices: Outside the building or inside between the lead-in entrance and the radio set or transformers, as near as practicable to the entrance
Only at the antenna’s highest point
Inside a hazardous location beside combustible material
At the farthest receptacle from the antenna
questions.answer: Outside the building or inside between the lead-in entrance and the radio set or transformers, as near as practicable to the entrance
questions.explanation: The antenna discharge unit location must follow this outside-or-inside arrangement and be as near as practicable to the entrance. Reference: 810.20(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Coaxial cable supplies power to equipment directly associated with its radio-frequency distribution system. What maximum voltage is permitted?
questions.explanation: Coaxial cable may deliver power to directly associated equipment if voltage is not over 60 volts and the source has power-limiting characteristics. Reference: 820.15, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: For a direct-buried network-powered broadband cable in a location not otherwise specified, what minimum cover is required?
questions.explanation: The minimum-cover table specifies 450 mm (18 in.) for direct-buried cable in locations not otherwise specified. Reference: Table 830.47(A), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: An ideal transformer has 800 primary turns and 200 secondary turns. If the secondary supplies 16 amperes, what current flows in the primary?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, Ip = Is × Ns ÷ Np = 16 × 200 ÷ 800 = 4 amperes. Reference: General trade theory — ideal transformer current ratio.

questions.question: A conductor carrying 7.5 amperes passes through a current-transformer window four times. What total ampere-turns does the current transformer see?
questions.explanation: Ampere-turns equal current multiplied by turns: 7.5 A × 4 turns = 30 ampere-turns. Reference: General trade theory — ampere-turn relationship.

questions.question: What effects can nonsinusoidal currents from nonlinear loads produce in a transformer?
choices: A guaranteed reduction in conductor temperature
questions.explanation: The transformer ventilation information notes that nonlinear loads with nonsinusoidal currents can result in additional losses and transformer heating. Reference: 450.9, Informational Note No. 2, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Why is the neutral of a four-wire, three-phase wye circuit counted as current carrying when the major portion of the load is nonlinear?
choices: Harmonic currents are present in the neutral conductor
The neutral always carries zero current
The phase conductors contain no current
questions.answer: Harmonic currents are present in the neutral conductor
questions.explanation: For this nonlinear-load arrangement, the NEC states that harmonic currents are present in the neutral, so it is current carrying. Reference: 310.15(E)(3), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: A 24-volt source is connected to 4-ohm and 8-ohm resistors in series. What current flows in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Series resistance is 4 + 8 = 12 ohms. Ohm’s law gives I = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 amperes. Reference: General trade theory — series resistance and Ohm’s law.

questions.question: Three parallel telecommunications devices each draw 0.8 ampere from the same source. What total current does the source supply?
questions.explanation: Parallel branch currents add: 0.8 + 0.8 + 0.8 = 2.4 amperes. Reference: General trade theory — Kirchhoff’s current law.
